central.state_why: the state keeps 36 credits of general education in law but lets up to 12 credits of major courses count toward it, as Louisiana does in its 90-hour Accelerated Baccalaureate (Louisiana Board of Regents AA Policy 2.15); the one rule with a precedent written for 90-credit degrees
central.accreditor_why: ACCE and ABET keep their numbers and all 17 ACCE Student Learning Outcomes but count a merged or AI-shortened course at the credits of what it replaces; both accreditors already judge programs by student outcomes, so counting competence changes how credit is read, not what graduates must show
central.finance_why: Florida law today: tuition per credit hour (s. 1009.24) and state allocation by planned enrollment (s. 1011.90(1))
central.ai_why: no change in teaching is the reference; the five AI futures of Module 18 and an AI ceiling are read against it
